newsitem.title: USA: Featherlite sees improved Q4 results.
newsitem.headline: Featherlite sees improved Q4 results.

text.p: Featherlite Mfg. Inc said Thursday that it expects its results for the fourth quarter to be higher than the $0.03 a share profit reported in the third quarter.

"The fourth quarter should be much better than 1995's which saw a loss," Conrad Clement, president, said in a statement. "Additionally, we expect the fourth quarter to be improved over this year's third quarter."
In the fourth quarter of 1995, Featherlite reported a loss of $0.06 a share, which included a $0.03 litigation settlement expense.

"Sales are expected to remain strong for the rest of the year in nearly all product groups," Clement said. "The recent Vantare acquisition will add significant luxury motorcoach sales in the final quarter of 1996 and into 1997. Increases in livestock trailer sales are expected to continue as cattle prices have improved."

Significant additional sales are expected during the last half of the year from the sale of private label snowmobile trailers, Featherlite said, and continued growth is expected in drop-frame delivery and moving van sales.
Clement said he expects drop frame and moving van sales to substantially replace sales of semi-flat bed trailers which the company discontinued due to lower profit margins.
Fourth quarter earnings should benefit from price increases announced July 1, which are effective on nearly all products to be delivered in the fourth quarter.
Sales backlog at September 30 was $32 million, up substantially from the year-ago backlog of $8.7 million.

Looking ahead, continued decreases in the average cost of aluminum will help gross margins, Clement said. "We have obtained commitments from suppliers to provide, at an agreed upon fixed price, substantial portions of our total aluminum requirements for the remainder of 1996 and much of 1997."
Featherlite, which makes specialty trailers, said the third quarter profit improved from a year-ago loss due to higher sales and declining aluminum costs.

"All of our product lines experienced dramatic growth with the exception of car trailer and race car transporters, which were down 10 percent for the quarter and three percent for the nine months," Clement said. "However, this product segment has significant backlog and we expect to make up the difference in the fourth quarter."
